text:
marcus: Quick Q on embeddings endpoint behavior — trying to finalise the contract for empty / very short inputs and truncation. TL;DR: what should we return for an empty string and for items that get fully truncated?

anya: Good call. We should be explicit. Current impl returns a zero vector for empty string, but I think that came from an ML fallback not the contract.

devin: @anya can you confirm where that diff lives? I remember a comment in the model adapter about zero-padding vs null.

anya: PR https://git.redwood/repo/infra/embeds-adapter/pull/412 — the adapter maps "" -> zeros currently (line ~128). It was a quick fix to avoid shape inconsistency in downstream batching.

marcus: Problem: SDKs expect 1:1 items -> vectors and some clients rely on numeric arrays (no nulls). But returning zeros silently could mask data issues. Would prefer explicit null for fully truncated inputs so caller can detect it.

sahil: If we switch to null, we break older SDKs that assume floats. Can we make it opt-in via a param like `return_nulls=true`?

devin: Implementation wise adding a query/body param is easy. But we should decide default for backward compatibility. Most users expect stable shape for array-of-embeddings. Breaking change is risky.

anya: Proposal: default stays zeros (back-compat). Add `nullable_items: true|false` in request JSON (default false). If true, we put `null` for fully-truncated items. Also add `truncation_policy` optional field: one of `truncate_tokens` (default), `truncate_chars`, `reject`.

marcus: I like explicit `truncation_policy`. For `reject` we return 400 with error code `input_truncated` and include which indices failed. That lets strict callers fail fast.

devin: Agreed. For response shape we should document the stable format: `data` is array of objects with `index` and `embedding` OR `null` when nullable. Example: 
```json
{ "model": "rwd-embed-v1", "data": [ { "index": 0, "embedding": [0.001, -0.12, ...] }, { "index": 1, "embedding": null } ] }
``` 
(embedding null only if `nullable_items=true`)

anya: Also need to decide: what about `input` being mixed types? e.g., `["str", [], null]`. We currently coerce non-strings to `""`. Should we keep coercion or return 400?

sahil: I'd prefer stricter validation: 400 with `invalid_input_type` pointing to indices. Coercion hides bugs. But again, breakage. Maybe deprecation: currently coerce, but warn in response header `X-Embeds-Coercion: true` and in next major bump make it an error.

marcus: OK plan: default zeros, add `nullable_items` flag, add `truncation_policy` (truncate_tokens|truncate_chars|reject), document response shape exactly, and deprecate coercion with warning header — then remove later.

devin: I'll draft the API spec changes and open PR for the router + runtime changes. @anya please update adapter to respect the `nullable_items` flag and `truncation_policy`.

anya: Will do. I'll also add unit tests for: empty string -> zeros (default), empty string -> null (nullable_items=true), rejected input -> 400 with indices array.

marcus: pinging @devin for code review when PR is up. Also add a small sample in SDKs showing how to handle nullable embeddings.

sdk-bot: Heads up: when PR lands, run `make regen-openapi` to push schema changes to SDK generator. (automated)

marcus: timeline: aim to have PRs by EOD Thu, deploy to staging Fri, and docs update next week. If anyone needs to opt into nullables earlier, raise here. :thumbsup:

sahil: quick note — perf: nullable nulls will still keep index entries so clients can align; no change to batch ordering. Good.

devin: creating the PR now: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/embeds-adapter/pull/427 (WIP) — will request @anya review.

marcus: thanks everyone. I'll update the design doc and drop a short note in #product later.
